reason: 1 application defect(s) reproduced by the evaluator: the AUT does not satisfy AC-5. Awaiting reviewer confirmation.

aut.name: ParaBank (Parasoft demo bank, UI + REST)
aut.notes: Shared demo DB that anyone can reset; register your own customer per test run. Behind Cloudflare: bursts of traffic are rate limited (Error 1015) or challenged, so tests run one worker at a time, at least 12 s apart.

applicationDefects.title: Wrong-password sign-in shows an internal-error message instead of 'The username and password could not be verified.'
applicationDefects.actual: element not found: getByText('The username and password could not be verified.')
applicationDefects.rationale: Signing in on the Customer Login panel with a registered user name and a wrong password reaches the 'Error!' page (as AC-5 requires), but the page says 'An internal error has occurred and has been logged.' instead of the required 'The username and password could not be verified.'. Locators are verified (heading 'Error!' found; the required text is absent). Deterministic: same result in every harden run, in 04-eval, 05/06/07-rerun and in two live replays. The REST login with the same credentials correctly answers 400 'Invalid username and/or password', so the customer exists and only the password is wrong.
applicationDefects.liveCheck: Replayed live 2026-09-27 (tier 3, heldout inspect): registered customer + wrong password on index.htm → heading 'Error!', text 'An internal error has occurred and has been logged.', required text 0 matches (runs/07-rerun/confirm/SCN-007-wrong-password.md); REST cross-check GET login/{user}/{wrong} → 400 'Invalid username and/or password' (runs/07-rerun/confirm/SCN-007-rest-wrong-password.md)
steps: Given a customer is registered with a fresh user name
And I am on the home page as a signed-out visitor
When I sign in on the Customer Login panel with that user name and a wrong password
And it says "The username and password could not be verified."
reproduce: npm run heldout -- run PB-1 --label repro --grep "SCN-007:"

traceability.text: Submitting the registration form with every field empty keeps the customer on the form and shows a message next to each required field: "First name is required.", "Last name is required.", "Address is required.", "City is required.", "State is required.", "Zip Code is required.", "Social Security Number is required.", "Username is required.", "Password is required.", "Password confirmation is required.". No message is shown for Phone #.

scenarios.title: Submitting an empty registration form shows a required message next to every required field

traceability.text: When Password and Confirm differ, the form shows "Passwords did not match." and no customer is created (the user name cannot sign in afterwards).

scenarios.title: Registering with a Confirm that differs from Password shows "Passwords did not match."
A registration rejected for mismatched passwords creates no customer

traceability.text: A complete, valid registration opens a page with the heading Welcome <username> (source: "Welcome _<username>_") and the text "Your account was created successfully. You are now logged in." The customer is signed in: the left panel greets them with Welcome <first name> <last name> (source: "Welcome _<first name> <last name>_") and shows the Account Services menu.

scenarios.title: A complete, valid registration welcomes the new customer and signs them in

traceability.text: Registering again with a user name that is already taken shows "This username already exists." next to Username and does not change the existing customer (a REST login of the existing customer still returns their original first and last name).

scenarios.title: Registering with a user name that is already taken shows "This username already exists."
A duplicate registration does not change the existing customer

traceability.text: On the Customer Login panel, signing in with a wrong password shows an "Error!" page with "The username and password could not be verified."; signing in with both fields empty shows "Please enter a username and password."

scenarios.title: Signing in with a wrong password shows the "Error!" page
Signing in with both fields empty asks for a user name and password

traceability.text: Signing in with the registered user name and password opens the Accounts Overview page, which lists at least one account for the new customer. "Log Out" returns to the home page with the Customer Login panel.

scenarios.title: Signing in opens the Accounts Overview and Log Out returns to the home page

traceability.text: GET /login/{username}/{password} with valid credentials answers 200 and returns the customer: id, firstName, lastName, address (street, city, state, zipCode) and phoneNumber, equal to the values entered at registration. With Accept: application/json the body is JSON; without it, XML with a customer root element.

scenarios.title: REST login with valid credentials returns the registered customer as JSON
REST login without Accept: application/json returns XML with a customer root element

traceability.text: GET /login/{username}/{password} with a wrong password answers 400 with the body "Invalid username and/or password".

scenarios.title: REST login with a wrong password answers 400 "Invalid username and/or password"

traceability.text: End to end: for a customer registered through the page, GET /customers/{id} (id from the login response) returns the same customer, and GET /customers/{id}/accounts returns the account(s) whose numbers are shown in the Accounts Overview.

scenarios.title: The customer and accounts services return the customer registered through the page
The customer and accounts services match the login response and the Accounts Overview exactly
